displayDescription: Glass neon tubes light one run at a time, from a source node through an idea bulb to the next node, reflected on a glossy floor.
styleRenderer: Three.js 0.187.0 (WebGL: swept TubeGeometry glass + emissive gas shaders, light-receiving wall and floor shaders, mirrored floor reflection, UnrealBloom)
audioDescription: Silent preview: no music, effects or narration.
limitations: STYLE.json lists no preview recipes and no BACKGROUND_REVIEW.json was supplied, so the preview demonstrates the catalogue's main characteristic action: connected tube runs light one contiguous section at a time, pause at each junction, and show their reflected shape on the floor.

Glass and gas are approximated with custom shaders (a Fresnel-edged clear sleeve around an emissive core), not physical refraction. The floor reflection is a mirrored copy of the sign under a semi-opaque glossy floor, not ray-traced. Light on the wall and floor comes from sampled points along each lit tube.
The second caption, 'SECTION 2 OF 2 LIT', is derived from the approved 'SECTION 1 OF 2 LIT' to mark the second run lighting up.
The headline and captions are crisp HTML text over the dark wall rather than bent tube lettering, so the approved copy stays readable.
Blender was not used, as instructed. Three.js and GSAP were copied from the existing local packages into the project runtime folder. Nothing was downloaded.
The bundled Three.js library contains Math.random and performance.now in internal utilities (object IDs and clocks). The scene never uses them; every visual value comes from the GSAP timeline time.
The technology-selection tool failed because a host-side PROJECT_DEPENDENCIES.json file is missing, so the dependency record may be incomplete. The runtime folder's package.json lists three and gsap.
